config.title: Default Props

intro.title: Default Props
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that displays a user's name and age. You will learn how to use default property values to ensure your component works even when certain data is not provided. The core concept involves setting default values for @Input() properties in Angular components. You will use TypeScript to define types and Angular's @Input() decorator to handle component properties. This approach makes your components more robust and easier to reuse in different parts of an application.
intro.usecase: Default props are essential in Angular when building reusable UI components that need consistent fallback values. In dashboard applications, chart components often use default props for initial settings like chart type, color schemes, or data refresh intervals. Form input components benefit from default props for placeholder text, validation rules, and error message templates. E-commerce product cards use default props for missing images, pricing formats, and 'out of stock' labels to maintain consistent presentation across catalog pages.

objectives: Initialize component properties with default values using TypeScript interfaces
Configure Angular components to accept optional inputs with fallback defaults
Apply default property values when parent components omit optional inputs
Construct reusable components that maintain consistent behavior with missing props
Update component templates to safely display properties with default fallbacks
Bind component logic to default values that activate when inputs are undefined
Integrate default props patterns to make components more robust and predictable

steps.title: Import Component and Input decorators from @angular/core
steps.instruction: Import the Component and Input decorators from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple named exports from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing decorators from Angular core
import { Component, Input } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component and Input decorators are imported and ready to be used in your Angular component.
successCriteria: Component and Input are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Component and Input from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is incorrect. You need to import both Component and Input from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main component class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction:
Create a class named 'DefaultPropsDemo' and decorate it with @Component. In the decorator metadata, set the selector to 'app-default-props-demo' and the template to a simple string like '

Default Props Demo

'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator imported in the previous step. The class should be exported so it can be used elsewhere.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, Input } from '@angular/core';

// Create the DefaultPropsDemo component class here
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named DefaultPropsDemo is created with basic metadata.
successCriteria: The DefaultPropsDemo class is defined, decorated with @Component, has selector 'app-default-props-demo', and includes a template string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the class is named DefaultPropsDemo, uses @Component with selector and template, and is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class is missing or incomplete. Check that you've defined the class, added the @Component decorator with selector and template, and exported it.

steps.title: Define an input property with @Input decorator
steps.instruction: Inside the DefaultPropsDemo component class, add an @Input() property named 'message' with type string.
steps.hint: Use the @Input() decorator before a property declaration to make it an input that can receive data from parent components.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has an input property that can receive a string value from a parent component.
successCriteria: The DefaultPropsDemo class contains an @Input() decorator applied to a property named 'message' with type string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've used the @Input() decorator and specified the type as string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input property isn't defined correctly. Check that you've used @Input() decorator and specified the type.

steps.title: Display the input property in the template
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add interpolation syntax {{ }} to display the value of the input property.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces with the property name inside to bind the value to the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will show the input property value when rendered.
successCriteria: The template contains interpolation syntax {{ }} with the input property name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct interpolation syntax {{ }} with the property name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required interpolation syntax. Try adding {{ propertyName }} to the template.

steps.title: Test the component without providing input value
steps.instruction: In the template of the DefaultPropsDemo component, add a usage of the component without providing any value to its input property.
steps.hint: Use the component selector as an HTML element in the template, but do not bind any value to the input property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: using a component without input binding
<app-default-props-demo></app-default-props-demo>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will now include a self-closing tag for the component, but no input value is passed, allowing you to observe the default behavior.
successCriteria: The template contains <app-default-props-demo> with no input binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the component selector correctly and not binding any value to the input property.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem to match the expected action. Try adding the component to its template without any input binding.

steps.title: Add a default value to the input property
steps.instruction: In the DefaultPropsDemo component class, initialize the @Input() property with a default value of 'Guest'.
steps.hint: Assign a default string value directly to the property after the @Input() decorator.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: setting a default value for an input property
@Input() userName: string = 'Anonymous';
steps.expectedOutcome: The input property now has a default value that will be used when no value is provided from the parent component.
successCriteria: The @Input() property is initialized with the string value 'Guest'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've assigned the exact default value 'Guest' to the property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The default value wasn't set correctly. Remember to initialize the property with the string 'Guest' after the @Input() decorator.

steps.title: Test the component with the default value
steps.instruction: Add a default value to the @Input() property in your component class.
steps.hint: Assign a default value directly to the property after the @Input() decorator.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: setting a default value for an input
@Input() message: string = 'Hello, World!';
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a default value assigned to its input property, which will be displayed when no input binding is provided.
successCriteria: The @Input() property has a default value assigned using TypeScript syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to assign a default value directly to the property after the @Input() decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input property doesn't have a default value yet. Remember to assign a value like `= 'Default Text'` after the property declaration.

steps.title: Pass a custom value to override the default
steps.instruction: In the parent component's template, bind a custom value to the input property to override the default.
steps.hint: Use property binding syntax [inputName]="value" in the parent template where you use the component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component will pass a custom value that overrides the default input value.
successCriteria: The component selector is used in a parent template with property binding providing a custom value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using property binding syntax [inputName]="value" in the parent template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The custom value wasn't properly passed. Check that you're using the correct property binding syntax in the parent component.

steps.title: Create a second input property with different default
steps.instruction: Add a second @Input() property named 'count' with a number type and a default value of 5.
steps.hint: Use the @Input() decorator followed by the property name with type annotation and an initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: another input with default
@Input() count: number = 5;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have two input properties with different default values.
successCriteria: The component contains a second @Input() property named 'count' of type number with default value 5.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input property, but check the name, type, or default value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second input property is missing or incorrect. Review the instruction.

steps.title: Display both input properties in the template
steps.instruction: Update the component's template to display both input properties with descriptive labels.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind each input property in the template. You can add labels like 'First input:' and 'Second input:' before each value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will show both input values with clear labels, demonstrating how default values work when inputs are not provided.
successCriteria: Template contains both input properties displayed with descriptive labels using interpolation syntax {{ }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both input properties are displayed in the template with clear labels.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't properly display both input properties. Remember to use interpolation {{ }} to show each property value.
